symbols.name: d
symbols.def: The number of observed scalar coordinates.

symbols.name: Part
symbols.def: The set of all partitions of \(V\) into nonempty blocks.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: The observational law of the coordinate vector.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: \(X=(X_v)_{v\in V}\) has law \(P\).

symbols.name: pP
symbols.def: \(p_P\) denotes the Lebesgue density of \(P\) on the admissible-model fiber; its existence, strict positivity, and formula are derived by the triangular observed-density lemma.

symbols.name: ellP
symbols.def: \(\ell_P=\log p_P\), where \(p_P\) is the density derived by the triangular observed-density lemma.

symbols.name: pi
symbols.def: A candidate partition of the observed coordinate labels.

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: A coordinate-labelled block graph whose vertices are the blocks of \(\pi\).

symbols.name: paG
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{pa}_G(B)\) is the parent-block set of \(B\) in \(G\).

symbols.name: ndG
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{nd}_G(B)\) is the set of nondescendant blocks of \(B\) in \(G\).

symbols.name: fBlock
symbols.def: For each \(B\in\pi\), \(f_B\) maps the coordinates in its parent blocks to the coordinates in \(B\).

symbols.name: epsBlock
symbols.def: The residual innovation attached to each block mechanism.

symbols.name: pEps
symbols.def: \(p_{\varepsilon_B}\) is the Lebesgue density of the block innovation \(\varepsilon_B\).

symbols.name: nuEps
symbols.def: The log-density of each block innovation.

symbols.name: mSlice
symbols.def: For a strictly positive bivariate Lebesgue density \(p\), \(m_p\) is its first-coordinate slice integral, defined as an extended nonnegative measurable function.

symbols.name: ESlice
symbols.def: The conull set of second-coordinate values on which the slice normalizer is positive and finite.

symbols.name: qSlice
symbols.def: The normalized first-coordinate slice, defined only on the regular set \(E_p\).

symbols.name: R
symbols.def: \(R=(\pi,G,(f_B)_{B\in\pi},(\varepsilon_B)_{B\in\pi})\) with \(X_B=f_B(X_{\cup\operatorname{pa}_G(B)})+\varepsilon_B\) for every \(B\in\pi\).

symbols.name: Rprime
symbols.def: \(R'\) is a second representation of the same law \(P\), with its own partition, graph, mechanisms, and innovations.

symbols.name: partOf
symbols.def: \(\pi_R\) is the coordinate partition carried by \(R\).

symbols.name: graphOf
symbols.def: \(G_R\) is the block DAG carried by \(R\), with its blocks labelled by coordinate subsets.

symbols.name: mechanismOf
symbols.def: \(f_{R,B}\) is the mechanism of block \(B\in\pi_R\).

symbols.name: innovationOf
symbols.def: \(\varepsilon_{R,B}\) is the innovation of block \(B\in\pi_R\).

symbols.name: ellCond
symbols.def: The conditional log-density of two disjoint coordinate blocks at a positive-density conditioning value.

symbols.name: AP
symbols.def: The admissible innovation-atomic grouped additive-noise representations of \(P\), defined in \(\mathrm{def:admissible-class}\).

symbols.name: preceq
symbols.def: \(\pi_1\preceq\pi_2\) means every block of \(\pi_1\) is contained in a block of \(\pi_2\).

symbols.name: meet
symbols.def: \(\pi_1\wedge\pi_2=\{B_1\cap B_2:B_1\in\pi_1,\ B_2\in\pi_2,\ B_1\cap B_2\neq\varnothing\}\).

symbols.name: TP
symbols.def: \(\mathcal T(P)=\{(\pi_R,G_R):R\in\mathfrak A(P)\}\), where graphs retain coordinate-subset labels.

symbols.name: pi0
symbols.def: A partition supplied externally before graph identification.

symbols.name: AGiven
symbols.def: The supplied-partition GANM fiber of Göbler, Windisch, and Drton, defined in \(\mathrm{def:supplied-group-class}\).

symbols.name: APeters
symbols.def: The scalar restricted-ANM fiber of Peters et al., defined in \(\mathrm{def:scalar-restricted-class}\).

symbols.name: Pmerge
symbols.def: The explicit nonlinear Gaussian merging witness defined in \(\mathrm{def:merge-witness}\).

symbols.name: mDim
symbols.def: \(m\) indexes Euclidean residual-law dimensions.

symbols.name: SmoothPos
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{SmoothPos}(m)\) is the residual-law class defined in \(\mathrm{def:smooth-positive-laws}\).

symbols.name: phiCond
symbols.def: For a random vector \(Z\) with a positive joint density and a split \(C\mathbin{\dot\cup}D\), \(\varphi_{D\mid C=c}\) is any regular version of the conditional characteristic function, defined for marginal-almost-every \(c\).

symbols.name: thetaVec
symbols.def: \(\theta=(a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda)\) indexes the explicit open five-parameter vector-innovation family; the coefficient labels \(c_0,d_0\) are distinguished from the ambient dimension \(d\).

symbols.name: Pvector
symbols.def: \(P_{\mathrm{vec},\theta}\) is the explicit genuinely vector innovation law defined in \(\mathrm{def:vector-atomic-witness}\).
symbols.role: open finite-dimensional strict scalar-frontier witness family

assumptions.condition: For every \(B\in\pi_R\), the mechanism \(f_{R,B}\) is three times continuously differentiable on its Euclidean domain.
For every \(B\in\pi_R\), the innovation \(\varepsilon_{R,B}\) has a Lebesgue density that is strictly positive on \(\mathbb R^{|B|}\).
For every \(B\in\pi_R\), the innovation log-density \(\nu_{R,B}\) belongs to \(C^3(\mathbb R^{|B|})\).

standard.name: Smooth block-noise log-density for vector ANM Condition 1

assumptions.condition: The coordinate-labelled block graph \(G_R\) is acyclic.
For every edge \(A\to B\) in \(G_R\), the mechanism \(f_{R,B}\) is nonconstant in the input coordinates indexed by \(A\).

On \(\pi_{\mathrm{sing}}\), for every node \(j\in V\), every parent \(i\in\operatorname{pa}_{G_R}(j)\), and every set \(S\) with \(\operatorname{pa}_{G_R}(j)\setminus\{i\}\subseteq S\subseteq\operatorname{nd}_{G_R}(j)\setminus\{i,j\}\), there exists \(x_S\) with \(p_{X_S}(x_S)>0\) such that \( igl(f_{R,j}(x_{\operatorname{pa}_{G_R}(j)\setminus\{i\}},\,\cdot),\mathcal L(X_i\mid X_S=x_S),\mathcal L(\varepsilon_{R,j}) igr)\) does not solve Equation (7) of Peters et al. for all \(x_i,x_j\) satisfying \(
u''(x_j-f(x_i))f'(x_i)
eq0\), with \(\xi=\log p_{X_i\mid X_S=x_S}\), \(
u=\log p_{\varepsilon_{R,j}}\), and \(f=f_{R,j}(x_{\operatorname{pa}_{G_R}(j)\setminus\{i\}},\,\cdot)\).

For every \(B\in\pi_R\) and every nontrivial split \(B=C\mathbin{\dot\cup}D\), for every \(C^3\) map \(h:\mathbb R^{|C|}\to\mathbb R^{|D|}\) and every random vector \(\eta_D\) with \(\mathcal L(\eta_D)\in\operatorname{SmoothPos}(|D|)\), the relation \(\varepsilon_{R,D}=h(\varepsilon_{R,C})+\eta_D\) almost surely with \(\eta_D\perp\!\!\!\perp\varepsilon_{R,C}\) does not hold and, symmetrically, for every \(C^3\) map \(k:\mathbb R^{|D|}\to\mathbb R^{|C|}\) and every random vector \(\eta_C\) with \(\mathcal L(\eta_C)\in\operatorname{SmoothPos}(|C|)\), the relation \(\varepsilon_{R,C}=k(\varepsilon_{R,D})+\eta_C\) almost surely with \(\eta_C\perp\!\!\!\perp\varepsilon_{R,D}\) does not hold.

novel.justification: Coordinate-level ANM irreducibility is the nonlinear causal analogue of irreducible independent subspaces. It is satisfied by the open five-parameter family with density proportional to \(\exp\{-(a u^4+b v^4+\lambda u^2v^2+c_0u^2+d_0v^2)\}\) for \(a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda>0\), as certified in both directions by strictly varying conditional variances.

definitions.name: Smooth positive residual-law class
definitions.construction: For every \(m\ge1\), \(\operatorname{SmoothPos}(m)=\{\mu\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^m):\mu\text{ has a Lebesgue density }r,\ r(x)>0\text{ for every }x\in\mathbb R^m,\ \int_{\mathbb R^m}r(x)\,dx=1,\text{ and }\log r\in C^3(\mathbb R^m)\}\).

definitions.name: Admissible innovation-atomic GANM fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak A(P)=\{R: R\text{ induces }P,\ f_{R,B}\in C^3,\ p_{\varepsilon_{R,B}}>0,\ \nu_{R,B}\in C^3,\ (\varepsilon_{R,B})_{B\in\pi_R}\text{ are mutually independent},\ G_R\text{ is acyclic and causally minimal, every parent--node--nondescendant triple satisfies the published Göbler--Windisch--Drton Equation (3)-failure condition, and every }\varepsilon_{R,B}\text{ is innovation-atomic}\}\).

definitions.name: Coordinate refinement order
definitions.construction: For \(\pi_1,\pi_2\in\operatorname{Part}(V)\), set \(\pi_1\preceq\pi_2\iff(\forall C\in\pi_1)(\exists B\in\pi_2)\ C\subseteq B\).

definitions.name: Atomic partition-and-DAG recovery map
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal T(P)=\{(\pi_R,G_R):R\in\mathfrak A(P)\}\), with equality of graphs requiring equality of the coordinate-subset vertex labels and directed edge sets.

definitions.name: Published supplied-partition GANM fiber
definitions.construction: For \(\pi_0\in\operatorname{Part}(V)\), \(\mathfrak G_{\pi_0}(P)=\{R:R\text{ induces }P,\ \pi_R=\pi_0,\ R\text{ is a GANM in the sense of Definition 2 of Göbler, Windisch, and Drton, }P\text{ satisfies their Definition 3 causal minimality, the mechanisms have the }C^3\text{ regularity used in their Section 2.2, and every parent--node--nondescendant conditional triple satisfies their Corollary 1 requirement by failing their Equation (3)}\}\).

definitions.name: Published scalar restricted-ANM fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak S(P)=\{R:R\text{ induces }P\text{ and is a restricted additive-noise model on }\pi_{\mathrm{sing}}\text{ in the exact sense of Definition 27 and Condition 19 of Peters et al., with the stated nonvanishing noise densities and }C^3\text{ mechanisms}\}\).

definitions.name: Nondescendant overlap-cell handle
definitions.construction: Starting from an incomparable pair \(R,R'\in\mathfrak A(P)\), choose a sink disagreement as in the nondescendant reduction of Peters et al., condition only on whole blocks that are nondescendants in both graphs, normalize the two conditional factorizations in a shared overlap coordinate, and differentiate their exact translation-family identity on the smallest nonempty cells of \(\pi_R\wedge\pi_{R'}\); propagate the local shifts across overlapping inversion charts and positive-density chart boundaries. Invoke the published Equation (3)-failure condition only for a conditional pair of whole supplied blocks.

definitions.name: Extremal finer-block quotient handle
definitions.construction: For \(R,R'\in\mathfrak A(P)\) with \(\pi_R\preceq\pi_{R'}\) and \(\pi_R\neq\pi_{R'}\), choose a coarse block \(B\in\pi_{R'}\) containing at least two blocks of \(\pi_R\), select an extremal finer block \(C\subsetneq B\) in a topological order of the finer-block DAG induced inside \(B\), and compare the two triangular density factorizations after cancelling or conditioning only on whole blocks external to \(B\). Prove a coarse-noise factorization or density-quotient lemma that turns the induced internal finer-block DAG into a directional representation \(\varepsilon_{R',B\setminus C}=h(\varepsilon_{R',C})+\eta_{B\setminus C}\) with \(h\in C^3\), \(\eta_{B\setminus C}\perp\!\!\!\perp\varepsilon_{R',C}\), and \(\mathcal L(\eta_{B\setminus C})\in\operatorname{SmoothPos}(|B\setminus C|)\), or the symmetric direction with residual law in \(\operatorname{SmoothPos}(|C|)\).

definitions.name: Three-coordinate translation-family handle
definitions.construction: For the crossing \(\{1,2\}\leftarrow\{3\}\) versus \(\{1,3\}\leftarrow\{2\}\), write \(f=(f_1,f_2)\) and \(g=(g_1,g_3)\), set \(v=x_2-f_2(x_3)\), \(z=x_3-g_3(x_2)\), and \(\delta=f_1(x_3)-g_1(x_2)\), and define conditional slices only on \(E_{p_\varepsilon}\) and \(E_{p_\eta}\). On each inverse chart of \(\Phi(x_2,x_3)=(v,z)\) inside \(\Omega=\{1-f_2'(x_3)g_3'(x_2)\neq0\}\), pull back these conull regular sets, divide the original positive factorization at \(t\) and a fixed \(t_0\), and differentiate only the resulting log-ratio identity. Derive overlap gluing and critical-set continuation from that identity, without differentiating a slice normalizer or conditional density, and analyze the identically singular Jacobian equation separately.

definitions.name: Nonlinear Gaussian block-merging witness
definitions.construction: Let \(N_1,N_2,N_3\) be independent standard Gaussian variables and set \(X_1=N_1\), \(X_2=X_1+X_1^3+N_2\), and \(X_3=N_3\). The law \(P_{\mathrm{merge}}\) has the singleton representation with the edge \(\{1\}\to\{2\}\) and the coarser empty-DAG representation with blocks \(\{1,2\}\) and \(\{3\}\).

definitions.name: Genuinely vector atomic innovation witness
definitions.construction: For \(\theta=(a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda)\in(0,\infty)^5\), define \(p_{a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda}(u,v)=Z_{a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda}^{-1}\exp\{-(a u^4+b v^4+\lambda u^2v^2+c_0u^2+d_0v^2)\}\), where \(Z_{a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda}=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\exp\{-(a u^4+b v^4+\lambda u^2v^2+c_0u^2+d_0v^2)\}\,du\,dv\). Let \(W\) be independent with density \(Z_W^{-1}\exp\{-(w^4+w^2)\}\), let \(P_{\mathrm{vec},\theta}\) be the law of \((U,V,W)\), and equip its empty DAG with blocks \(\{1,2\}\) and \(\{3\}\).

statements.statement: If \(\mu\in\operatorname{SmoothPos}(m)\), then every nonempty Euclidean open set has positive \(\mu\)-probability. In particular, \(\mu\) is not supported on any proper affine subspace of \(\mathbb R^m\). Thus full density positivity already implies nondegeneracy; nondegeneracy is not an additional residual-law condition.
statements.justification: The lemma removes an undefined adjective from every innovation split and records the exact implication supplied by full support.
statements.gap: The grouped ANM comparators assume positive noise densities but do not package the resulting affine nondegeneracy as the residual-law quantifier needed for innovation atomicity.
statements.consumer: All crossing and refinement rigidity statements can quantify only over \(\operatorname{SmoothPos}\) residuals without a separate nondegeneracy clause.

statements.statement: Let \(Z=(Z_j)_{j\in B}\) have a strictly positive joint Lebesgue density with \(\log p_Z\in C^3(\mathbb R^{|B|})\). For each nontrivial split \(B=C\mathbin{\dot\cup}D\), suppose there exist \(t_D\in\mathbb R^{|D|}\), measurable sets \(A_1,A_2\subseteq\mathbb R^{|C|}\) with \(P_{Z_C}(A_j)>0\), and constants \(0\le\alpha_D<\beta_D\le1\) such that \( |\varphi_{D\mid C=c}(t_D)|\le\alpha_D\) for \(P_{Z_C}\)-almost every \(c\in A_1\) and \( |\varphi_{D\mid C=c}(t_D)|\ge\beta_D\) for \(P_{Z_C}\)-almost every \(c\in A_2\). Suppose symmetrically that there exist \(t_C\), positive-\(P_{Z_D}\)-measure sets \(H_1,H_2\), and \(0\le\alpha_C<\beta_C\le1\) separating \( |\varphi_{C\mid D=d'}(t_C)|\) on \(H_1,H_2\). Then neither directional additive-noise representation is possible and \(Z\) is innovation-atomic. Indeed, \(Z_D=h(Z_C)+\eta_D\) with independent \(\eta_D\) would imply \( |\varphi_{D\mid C=c}(t)|=|\varphi_{\eta_D}(t)|\) for marginal-almost every \(c\), and the reverse direction gives the symmetric constant-modulus consequence.
statements.justification: This gives a directly observable sufficient criterion for the existential exclusion in innovation atomicity.
statements.gap: Scalar ANM diagnostics test directionality for a prescribed pair, whereas the criterion is organized split-by-split to certify irreducibility of a proposed multivariate causal unit.
statements.consumer: A multichannel block can be screened for internal directional ANMs using conditional distribution shape rather than fitting every possible mechanism.

statements.statement: In the setting of Proposition 1, assume finite second moments. For a fixed split \(B=C\mathbin{\dot\cup}D\), if the matrix \(\operatorname{Cov}(Z_D\mid Z_C=c)\) is not essentially constant in \(c\), then no representation \(Z_D=h(Z_C)+\eta_D\) with an independent residual is possible; the symmetric statement holds with \(C\) and \(D\) interchanged. If both directional covariance-variation conclusions hold for every nontrivial split, they suffice for innovation atomicity. This covariance test is sufficient for directional falsification but not necessary: failure to detect variation, including an essentially constant conditional covariance, does not certify atomicity.
statements.justification: Conditional covariance is an easily checked finite-moment implication of the stronger location-family restriction.
statements.gap: Park2020 is a distinct scalar-node multivariate-DAG result based on conditional-variance orderings across nodes, whereas this elementary result is only a one-direction covariance-variation falsification diagnostic for a prescribed block split and is not an admissibility premise.
statements.consumer: The diagnostic supplies an interpretable first pass for process blocks while retaining the characteristic-function criterion when moments are unreliable.

statements.statement: Let \(R\in\mathfrak A(P)\), and order its blocks topologically as \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\). The residual map \(\Psi_R:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) defined blockwise by \(\Psi_R(x)_{B_j}=x_{B_j}-f_{R,B_j}(x_{\cup\operatorname{pa}_{G_R}(B_j)})\) is a global \(C^3\) diffeomorphism: its inverse is obtained recursively along the topological order, its block Jacobian is triangular with identity diagonal blocks, and \(\det D\Psi_R(x)=1\) for every \(x\). Therefore the induced observational law has the density \[p_P(x)=\prod_{B\in\pi_R}p_{\varepsilon_{R,B}}\!\left(x_B-f_{R,B}(x_{\cup\operatorname{pa}_{G_R}(B)})\right)>0,\qquad \ell_P(x)=\sum_{B\in\pi_R}\nu_{R,B}\!\left(x_B-f_{R,B}(x_{\cup\operatorname{pa}_{G_R}(B)})\right)\in C^3(\mathbb R^d).\] Thus strict positivity and \(C^3\) regularity of the observed density are derived from acyclicity, the \(C^3\) mechanisms, and the mutually independent strictly positive \(C^3\) innovation log-densities.
statements.justification: The change-of-variables calculation removes observable density regularity from the admissible fiber and records it as a consequence of the structural model.
statements.gap: Grouped ANM work routinely writes the product factorization, but this lemma isolates the global triangular diffeomorphism and unit Jacobian needed to prevent observed smoothness and positivity from becoming circular premises here.
statements.consumer: Every density-intersection and conditional-factorization argument can invoke one derived observable-density result instead of assuming the regularity of \(P\).

statements.statement: If \(R,R'\in\mathfrak A(P)\) and both \(G_R\) and \(G_{R'}\) are empty, then the positive density \(p_P\) factorizes over every cell of \(\pi_R\wedge\pi_{R'}\). Consequently, if \(\pi_R\neq\pi_{R'}\), at least one block innovation in \(R\) or \(R'\) admits a nontrivial coordinate split with a zero \(C^3\) mechanism and an independent residual whose law belongs to the appropriate \(\operatorname{SmoothPos}\) class; therefore \(\pi_R=\pi_{R'}\).
statements.justification: This isolates the part of partition uniqueness supplied by positive-density intersection and shows exactly where causal mechanisms create the new difficulty.
statements.gap: GutchTheis2012 proves uniqueness for linear independent-subspace factorizations, but it does not treat a fixed observed coordinate system with causal mechanisms between blocks.
statements.consumer: The lemma settles unknown atomic grouping for independent multivariate shocks and supplies the base case for induction over block-DAG sinks.

statements.statement:
Let \(d=3\). Suppose \(R,R'\in\mathfrak A(P)\), \(\pi_R=\{\{1,2\},\{3\}\}\), \(\pi_{R'}=\{\{1,3\},\{2\}\}\), \(G_R\) has the single edge \(\{3\}	o\{1,2\}\), and \(G_{R'}\) has the single edge \(\{2\}	o\{1,3\}\). Write \(f=(f_1,f_2)\), \(g=(g_1,g_3)\), \(\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\), and \(\eta=(\eta_1,\eta_3)\) for the two nonroot mechanisms and innovations, and let \(r\) and \(s\) denote the strictly positive \(C^3\) marginal densities of \(X_3\) and \(X_2\), respectively. The triangular density formula gives, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^3\), \[r(x_3)p_{\varepsilon}(x_1-f_1(x_3),x_2-f_2(x_3))=s(x_2)p_{\eta}(x_1-g_1(x_2),x_3-g_3(x_2)).\] Set \(v=x_2-f_2(x_3)\), \(z=x_3-g_3(x_2)\), and \(\delta(x_2,x_3)=f_1(x_3)-g_1(x_2)\). Define the extended slice normalizers and regular sets \[m_{\varepsilon}(v)=\int_{\mathbb R}p_{\varepsilon}(t,v)\,dt,\quad E_{\varepsilon}=\{v:0<m_{\varepsilon}(v)<\infty\},\qquad m_{\eta}(z)=\int_{\mathbb R}p_{\eta}(t,z)\,dt,\quad E_{\eta}=\{z:0<m_{\eta}(z)<\infty\}.\] Tonelli's theorem, \(\int p_{\varepsilon}=\int p_{\eta}=1\), and strict positivity imply that \(E_{\varepsilon}\) and \(E_{\eta}\) are conull. Define \(q_{\varepsilon}(t\mid v)=p_{\varepsilon}(t,v)/m_{\varepsilon}(v)\) only for \(v\in E_{\varepsilon}\), and define \(q_{\eta}(t\mid z)=p_{\eta}(t,z)/m_{\eta}(z)\) only for \(z\in E_{\eta}\). The normalized translation identity is \[q_{\varepsilon}(t\mid v)=q_{\eta}(t+\delta(x_2,x_3)\mid z),\qquad t\in\mathbb R,\quad (x_2,x_3)\in D:=\Phi^{-1}(E_{\varepsilon}	imes E_{\eta}),\] where \(\Phi(x_2,x_3)=(v,z)\). Let \(\Omega=\{(x_2,x_3):1-f_2'(x_3)g_3'(x_2)
eq0\}\). It is open, and on every connected inverse chart \(U\subseteq\Omega\), \(\Phi|_U\) is a \(C^3\) diffeomorphism onto its open image and \(D_U=U\cap D\) is conull in \(U\), hence dense. Fix \(t_0\in\mathbb R\). Dividing the original positive factorization at \(t\) and \(t_0\), then taking logarithms, gives on \(D_U\) the identity \[
u_{\varepsilon}(t,v)-
u_{\varepsilon}(t_0,v)=
u_{\eta}(t+\delta,z)-
u_{\eta}(t_0+\delta,z).\] Continuity extends this log-ratio identity to every point of \(U\); only this extended identity, not \(m_{\varepsilon}\), \(m_{\eta}\), \(q_{\varepsilon}\), or \(q_{\eta}\), is differentiated. The extended identity implies the following chart and continuation conclusions. On each \(U\), there are \(C^3\) shift functions \(h_U\) and \(k_U\), normalized by \(h_U(v_U^0)=0\) at a regular base point, and a fixed smooth positive unit-integral profile chosen from one regular slice, such that the two regular conditional families are its translates and \(\delta=k_U(z)-h_U(v)\) on \(D_U\). On overlaps, the log-ratio identity forces any two normalized shift pairs to differ by one common additive constant; transport along every overlap chain is path independent. For any \(y\in\Omega^c\) approached by nonsingular charts, the same identity forces overlap-chain-independent limits of the shift differences and locally uniform limits of the translated log-density ratios and their first two \(t\)-derivatives, yielding a unique continuation through the critical set. These chart-gluing and critical-set statements are conclusions to be derived from the displayed log-ratio identity, not regularity assumptions on slice normalizers. They produce global \(C^3\) functions \(h,k\) and variables \(\zeta,\zeta'\) with \(\mathcal L(\zeta),\mathcal L(\zeta')\in\operatorname{SmoothPos}(1)\) such that \(\varepsilon_1=h(\varepsilon_2)+\zeta\), \(\zeta\perp\!\!\!\perp\varepsilon_2\), and \(\eta_1=k(\eta_3)+\zeta'\), \(\zeta'\perp\!\!\!\perp\eta_3\). If \(\Omega=\varnothing\), then \(f_2(x_3)=ax_3+c\) and \(g_3(x_2)=a^{-1}x_2+d_0\) for some \(a
eq0\), so \(\eta_3=-a^{-1}\varepsilon_2-a^{-1}c-d_0\); independence of \(X_2=aX_3+c+\varepsilon_2\) from \(\eta_3\), with \(X_3\perp\!\!\!\perp\varepsilon_2\), would make \(\varepsilon_2\), whose strictly positive density gives full support, independent of its sum with an independent variable, which is impossible. Thus either regime forces a nontrivial directional innovation split, and the two crossed representations cannot both be innovation-atomic.
statements.justification: This closes the smallest crossed-partition configuration by exposing the exact conditional identity and both the nonsingular and identically singular Jacobian regimes.
statements.gap: HoyerEtAl2008 treats two scalar directions and GoblerWindischDrton2025 treats disjoint supplied blocks; neither derives this overlap-conditioned translation identity for crossed vector innovations.
statements.consumer: Failure of this theorem produces the prescribed early counterexample and stops the global identification kernel before any arbitrary-block induction is attempted.

statements.statement: For arbitrary \(R,R'\in\mathfrak A(P)\), can the nondescendant overlap-cell handle extend the three-coordinate translation-family argument to prove that incomparable partitions \(\pi_R\) and \(\pi_{R'}\) force a nontrivial directional additive-noise split of some \(\varepsilon_{R,B}\) or \(\varepsilon_{R',B'}\) with a \(C^3\) mechanism, independence from the conditioning innovation coordinates, and residual law in the dimension-matched \(\operatorname{SmoothPos}\) class? Equivalently, establish that \(\pi_R\preceq\pi_{R'}\) or \(\pi_{R'}\preceq\pi_R\) by reducing an arbitrary minimal overlap crossing to charts on which whole nondescendant blocks can be conditioned without cutting through the competing innovation.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level bottleneck: conditioning for one representation may select coordinates from a correlated innovation of the competing representation.
statements.gap: PetersEtAl2014 localizes graph disagreement only when the scalar vertices are common, and GoblerWindischDrton2025 assumes the vector partition is supplied; neither controls overlap cells from crossed partitions.
statements.consumer: A positive solution rules out every higher-dimensional incomparable atomic grouping and turns the three-coordinate obstruction into a global partition-identification theorem.

statements.statement: Let \(R,R'\in\mathfrak A(P)\) have strictly comparable partitions, with \(\pi_R\preceq\pi_{R'}\) and \(\pi_R\neq\pi_{R'}\). Can one prove that some coarse block \(B\in\pi_{R'}\) contains at least two blocks of \(\pi_R\) and has a nontrivial coordinate split \(B=C\mathbin{\dot\cup}D\) for which its coarse innovation admits a directional \(C^3\) additive-noise representation \(\varepsilon_{R',D}=h(\varepsilon_{R',C})+\eta_D\), where \(h:\mathbb R^{|C|}\to\mathbb R^{|D|}\), \(\eta_D\perp\!\!\!\perp\varepsilon_{R',C}\), and \(\mathcal L(\eta_D)\in\operatorname{SmoothPos}(|D|)\), or \(\varepsilon_{R',C}=k(\varepsilon_{R',D})+\eta_C\), where \(k:\mathbb R^{|D|}\to\mathbb R^{|C|}\), \(\eta_C\perp\!\!\!\perp\varepsilon_{R',D}\), and \(\mathcal L(\eta_C)\in\operatorname{SmoothPos}(|C|)\)? Establish this split by comparing the two triangular factorizations, choosing an extremal finer block inside \(B\), cancelling or conditioning only on whole external blocks, and proving a coarse-noise factorization or density-quotient lemma that reduces the induced internal finer-block DAG to one of the displayed directions. Either direction contradicts innovation atomicity of the coarse representation.
statements.justification: Crossing rigidity yields only comparability; strict-refinement rigidity is the separate argument needed to prevent a coarser atomic unit from hiding a finer internal causal DAG.
statements.gap: Independent-subspace irreducibility excludes refinements for empty DAGs, while supplied-group GANM identification keeps the block partition fixed; no cited result converts a strictly finer competing causal factorization into an internal ANM split of the coarse innovation.
statements.consumer: Together with crossing rigidity, this obligation excludes every unequal competing partition and licenses equality rather than mere comparability in the population recovery map.

statements.statement: For every \(P\) and every \(R,R'\in\mathfrak A(P)\), the following partition-ambiguity frontier holds. First, \(\pi_R=\pi_{R'}\) implies \(G_R=G_{R'}\). Second, if \(G_R\) and \(G_{R'}\) are both empty, then \(\pi_R=\pi_{R'}\). Third, when \(d=3\), there are no distinct \(i,j,k\in V\) for which \(\pi_R=\{\{i,j\},\{k\}\}\), \(G_R\) has the single edge \(\{k\}\to\{i,j\}\), \(\pi_{R'}=\{\{i,k\},\{j\}\}\), and \(G_{R'}\) has the single edge \(\{j\}\to\{i,k\}\). Fourth, no such pair can satisfy \(\pi_R\preceq\pi_{R'}\), \(\pi_R\neq\pi_{R'}\), and possess a block \(B\in\pi_{R'}\) that is a root of \(G_{R'}\), contains at least two blocks of \(\pi_R\), and has the property that every \(G_R\)-parent of every block \(A\in\pi_R\) with \(A\subseteq B\) is itself contained in \(B\); the symmetric conclusion holds after interchanging \(R\) and \(R'\). These conclusions do not assert equality of arbitrary admissible partitions.
statements.justification: The theorem gives the exact population ambiguity frontier supported by the current assumptions, including conditional DAG uniqueness and three concrete cross-partition exclusions.
statements.gap: Published GANM and scalar ANM theorems fix their vertex partition; no located result excludes arbitrary crossed blocks or refinements with external fine parents.
statements.consumer: Joint grouping-and-graph algorithms can use these conclusions as necessary population checks while treating the remaining partition alternatives as an identified set.

statements.statement: For every \(P\), put \(\mathcal D_P=\{\pi_R:R\in\mathfrak A(P)\}\). There is a unique function \(\Gamma_P\) on \(\mathcal D_P\) such that \(G_R=\Gamma_P(\pi_R)\) for every \(R\in\mathfrak A(P)\), and hence \[\mathcal T(P)=\{(\pi,\Gamma_P(\pi)):\pi\in\mathcal D_P\}.\] Thus \(\mathcal T(P)\) is the graph of a partial function from coordinate partitions to coordinate-labelled block DAGs. Its domain obeys three proved exclusions: distinct domain points cannot both carry empty DAGs; when \(d=3\), it cannot contain the relabelled crossed single-edge pair \(\{\{i,j\},\{k\}\}\) and \(\{\{i,k\},\{j\}\}\); and it cannot contain a strict refinement pair satisfying the displayed coarse-root and fine-parent-closure conditions of the partition-ambiguity frontier. No claim is made that \(\mathcal D_P\) is a singleton.
statements.justification: The observable recovery relation is identified as one labelled DAG for each admissible partition, with its remaining partition ambiguity stated rather than hidden.
statements.gap: GoblerWindischDrton2025 identifies the DAG after a partition is supplied and does not prove that the admissible-partition domain is a singleton.
statements.consumer: Joint-learning procedures can compare their outputs against the graph-valued identified set and the three proved exclusion constraints.

statements.statement: For every \(\theta=(a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda)\in(0,\infty)^5\), the normalizer \(Z_{a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda}\) is finite and strictly positive, so \(p_{a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda}\) is a unit-integral, everywhere positive density with \(\log p_{a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda}\in C^3(\mathbb R^2)\); hence its law belongs to \(\operatorname{SmoothPos}(2)\). The mixed derivative \(\partial_{uv}\log p_{a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda}=-4\lambda uv\) is not identically zero, so \(U\) and \(V\) are dependent. Conditional on \(U=u\), the symmetric density of \(V\) is proportional to \(\exp\{-b v^4-rv^2\}\) with \(r=d_0+\lambda u^2\); writing expectation under this density as \(\mathbb E_r\), \[\frac{d}{dr}\operatorname{Var}(V\mid U=u)=\frac{d}{dr}\mathbb E_r[V^2]=-\operatorname{Var}_r(V^2)<0.\] Thus \(\operatorname{Var}(V\mid U=u)\) varies strictly with \(u^2\), excluding every \(V=h(U)+\eta_D\) with \(\eta_D\perp\!\!\!\perp U\). Symmetrically, the conditional density of \(U\) given \(V=v\) has quadratic coefficient \(c_0+\lambda v^2\), and \(d\mathbb E_s[U^2]/ds=-\operatorname{Var}_s(U^2)<0\), excluding every \(U=k(V)+\eta_C\) with \(\eta_C\perp\!\!\!\perp V\). The bivariate innovation is therefore atomic under the exact \(\operatorname{SmoothPos}\) residual-law definition. With the independent \(W\) specified in the vector-atomic witness definition, the empty-DAG representation with blocks \(\{1,2\}\) and \(\{3\}\) belongs to \(\mathfrak A(P_{\mathrm{vec},\theta})\) for every \(\theta\in(0,\infty)^5\). This is an open parameter family inside the displayed exponential-polynomial model, not an open set in the space of all densities and not a genericity assertion.
statements.justification: The open five-parameter family supplies direct normalization, dependence, smoothness, and two-direction atomicity calculations for genuinely vector shocks.
statements.gap: Conditional-variance ANM restrictions are used here to verify irreducibility of an explicit vector innovation family, not to replace the published Göbler Condition 1 or to assert genericity.
statements.consumer: It certifies the strict non-scalar witness in the Peters comparator frontier with a check valid at every point of an open Euclidean parameter set.

statements.statement: The published comparator frontier consists of the following fixed-partition and representational statements. First, for every supplied \(\pi_0\), \(\{R\in\mathfrak A(P):\pi_R=\pi_0\}\subseteq\mathfrak G_{\pi_0}(P)\); consequently, if \(R,R'\in\mathfrak A(P)\) have \(\pi_R=\pi_{R'}=\pi_0\), then \(G_R=G_{R'}\) by the fixed-partition theorem of Göbler, Windisch, and Drton. This inclusion is strict over law--representation pairs because the \(\{1,2\}|\{3\}\) empty-DAG representation of \(P_{\mathrm{merge}}\) belongs to the supplied-group fiber and fails innovation atomicity. Second, if \(R,R'\in\mathfrak A(P)\cap\mathfrak S(P)\), then \(G_R=G_{R'}\), agreeing on this common singleton subfiber with Theorem 28 of Peters et al. Third, for every \(\theta\in(0,\infty)^5\), \(\mathfrak A(P_{\mathrm{vec},\theta})\neq\varnothing\) and \(\mathfrak S(P_{\mathrm{vec},\theta})=\varnothing\). Thus the atomic class contains genuinely vector laws outside the scalar restricted-ANM class. These comparisons neither identify the unknown partition nor equate the vector Equation (3) with the scalar Equation (7).
statements.justification: The comparison now states only exact fixed-partition reductions, strict inclusion via the merging witness, and the explicit non-scalar family frontier.
statements.gap: The cited results fix grouped or scalar vertices, and none supports an unknown-partition uniqueness claim.
statements.consumer: A referee can audit the class inclusion, the common-fiber DAG agreement, and the genuinely vector family separately.

statements.statement: When the unique partition is supplied in advance, the atomic partition-and-DAG theorem reduces to fixed-group GANM DAG identification under the exact Corollary 1 Equation (3)-failure condition. On the common singleton subfiber that also satisfies Definition 27 of PetersEtAl2014, its graph conclusion agrees with scalar restricted-ANM DAG identification. In the empty-DAG case it reduces to uniqueness of the finest independent coordinate partition under innovation atomicity.
statements.justification: These reductions are mandatory sanity checks on the new partition-identification layer.
statements.gap: PetersEtAl2014 and GoblerWindischDrton2025 cover the common singleton and supplied-block reductions but not the unknown-partition conclusion.
statements.consumer: Existing RESIT and GroupRESIT population guarantees become corollaries under their respective fixed grouping regimes.

statements.statement: For \(P_{\mathrm{merge}}\), the singleton representation and the representation with blocks \(\{1,2\}\) and \(\{3\}\) satisfy every admissibility condition except innovation atomicity and induce the same smooth positive law, but their partitions differ. In the coarser representation, \(\varepsilon_{\{1,2\},2}=\varepsilon_{\{1,2\},1}+\varepsilon_{\{1,2\},1}^3+N_2\) is a directional \(C^3\) additive-noise split and \(\mathcal L(N_2)\in\operatorname{SmoothPos}(1)\). The singleton nonlinear Gaussian edge satisfies the applicable scalar instance of the published Equation (3)-failure requirement. Removing \(\mathrm{ass:innovation-atomicity}\) therefore destroys partition identification without altering the exact edgewise comparator condition.
statements.justification: This same-class witness shows that atomicity is identifying content rather than convenient terminology.
statements.gap: GutchTheis2012 gives the linear independent-subspace analogue, but no published grouped ANM result isolates coordinate innovation atomicity by a causal nonlinear witness.
statements.consumer: Practitioners can interpret a detected internal ANM as decisive evidence that a proposed process block is too coarse.

sampling_model.design: Population observational identification from the exact law \(P\); no intervention or assignment design is used.
sampling_model.units: One observed random vector \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) with scalar coordinate labels \(V\).
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment or outcome; the target is the causal-unit partition and its labelled block DAG.
sampling_model.overlap: Every admissible block innovation has a strictly positive Lebesgue density on its Euclidean space; the triangular observed-density lemma derives the strictly positive density of the observable law.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the proposal concerns identification from the exact population law \(P\).

target_estimand: \(\mathcal T(P)=\{(\pi,\Gamma_P(\pi)):\pi\in\mathcal D_P\}\), where \(\mathcal D_P=\{\pi_R:R\in\mathfrak A(P)\}\) and \(\Gamma_P\) is the uniquely identified labelled-DAG map on this domain; the domain is not claimed to be a singleton.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The graph \(\mathcal G_0\) is identifiable from the joint distribution \(P_{\mathbf X}\).
If a distribution is generated by a restricted additive-noise model that is causally minimal, then the corresponding directed acyclic graph is identifiable from the distribution.
We assume that all variables in \(\mathbf x\) are observed, and that the grouping of these variables is known.
Such a representation is unique up to trivial indeterminacies.
We propose a new scoring function, the Clustering Information Criterion.
We learn an approximate posterior over clusters and graph-structure.

tldr: Acyclic grouped additive-noise mechanisms with mutually independent innovation laws in \(\operatorname{SmoothPos}\) induce a strictly positive \(C^3\) observed density by a triangular unit-Jacobian change of variables. Innovation atomicity now quantifies exactly over both directional \(C^3\) additive-noise representations and residual laws in the dimension-matched \(\operatorname{SmoothPos}\) class; full positivity itself implies affine nondegeneracy. The sole new identification kernel has two separate obligations: crossing rigidity excludes incomparable partitions, while strict-refinement rigidity converts every proper refinement or coarsening into a forbidden internal split. The conull-slice three-coordinate theorem remains the early kill test. A conditional characteristic-function modulus criterion gives an observable sufficient certificate for atomicity, with conditional covariance variation only a sufficient directional diagnostic. The five-parameter density \(p_{a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda}(u,v)\propto\exp\{-(a u^4+b v^4+\lambda u^2v^2+c_0u^2+d_0v^2)\}\) is normalized and atomic for every positive parameter vector by strict conditional-variance variation. Once both global rigidity obligations are proved, partition recovery composes with Corollary 1 of GoblerWindischDrton2025; no finite certificate or genericity claim is made.

project_justification.gap: Göbler, Windisch, and Drton identify a GANM DAG only after the vector partition is supplied, while Peters et al. identify a restricted ANM DAG only on supplied scalar vertices. Entner and Hoyer assume known groups in a linear model with mutually independent group disturbances, use non-Gaussianity for their LiNGAM-based guarantees, and recover a causal order rather than a coordinate partition. Wahl, Ninad, and Runge leave joint partition-and-graph learning open, and the joint-learning algorithms of Niu, Li, and Li and Rajpal et al. do not exclude a second unequal population partition, whether crossed or strictly finer.
project_justification.niche: The positive smooth density derived from the triangular structural map gives an intersection argument for two empty-DAG factorizations, while conditional location families imply constant characteristic-function modulus. The missing identification objects are an arbitrary-block crossing theorem for incomparable partitions and a distinct quotient theorem turning a strict refinement into an internal coarse-innovation ANM.
project_justification.fill: The project derives observed-density positivity and \(C^3\) regularity from the triangular structural map. It fixes the residual-law quantifier as \(\operatorname{SmoothPos}(m)\), proves that full positivity implies affine nondegeneracy, and supplies a splitwise characteristic-function modulus criterion for atomicity; finite-moment covariance variation is retained only as a sufficient directional diagnostic whose failure to detect variation proves nothing. The three-coordinate crossing uses conull regular slices and differentiates only a continuous log-ratio identity. The nondescendant overlap-cell and extremal finer-block quotient handles address incomparable and strictly comparable partitions separately. The labelled DAG then follows from the cited fixed-partition theorem using the published Equation (3). The comparator frontier uses the open family \((a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda)\in(0,\infty)^5\), with normalization, dependence, and both directional exclusions proved by conditional-variance monotonicity.

related_work: HoyerEtAl2008 derives the scalar log-density differential obstruction and discusses the linear-Gaussian reversible boundary. PetersEtAl2014, Example 24, explicitly obtains the backward additive-noise model by Gaussian linear regression; this is retained only as a cited external regression fact. PetersEtAl2014, Condition 19, Definition 27, and Theorem 28, identifies a causally minimal restricted ANM DAG on a supplied scalar vertex set. The headline agrees with that conclusion on the common singleton subfiber; no equivalence is asserted between Peters et al.'s Equation (7) and the later vector Equation (3). The open five-parameter family \(p_{a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda}(u,v)\propto\exp\{-(a u^4+b v^4+\lambda u^2v^2+c_0u^2+d_0v^2)\}\), \((a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda)\in(0,\infty)^5\), lies beyond the scalar model because both directional conditional variances vary strictly with the squared conditioning coordinate. GoblerWindischDrton2025, Definition 2, Condition 1 and Equation (3) on page 1455, and Corollary 1 on page 1456, identifies the graph for a supplied vector partition. The admissible and supplied-group fibers use that full equation with the corollary's node--parent--nondescendant quantifiers; no separate Hessian-rank or derivative-ratio condition is imposed. The usual GANM product factorization is made explicit here as a triangular unit-Jacobian lemma, so positivity and \(C^3\) regularity of the observed density are derived from the structural primitives rather than added to the admissible fiber. Fixed-partition DAG identification is retained only as the cited Corollary 1 composition fact, while the sole new identification step is recovery of the partition itself. EntnerHoyer2012, Section 2 and Algorithm 1, assumes that the grouping is known, studies linear block equations with disturbances independent across groups and potentially dependent within groups, and estimates a causal order; its LiNGAM-based exogenous-group criterion assumes non-Gaussian disturbances, and it neither identifies an innovation-atomic coordinate partition nor proves a nonlinear block-DAG uniqueness theorem. The nonlinear merging witness makes the supplied-group inclusion strict. GutchTheis2012 supplies the irreducibility analogue for linear independent subspaces but has no causal DAG or crossed nonlinear mechanisms; its empty-DAG decomposition argument does not provide the coarse-noise quotient needed when a strict refinement carries internal causal edges. WahlNinadRunge2024 studies Markov and faithfulness transfer under a fixed partition and identifies joint partition--graph learning as challenging. NiuLiLi2022 uses total correlation, mutual information, an MDL penalty, and greedy C-DAG search. RajpalEtAl2026 instead optimizes a variational ELBO over categorical clusters and Bernoulli ordered edges for Gaussian vector SCM likelihoods. Neither algorithm proves recovery of the innovation-atomic population target. Park2020 is a distinct scalar-node multivariate-DAG result: its conditional-variance orderings compare nodes with ancestors or descendants to recover a causal order and graph. It does not orient a prescribed pair by conditional covariance variation. Here conditional covariance variation is only a sufficient diagnostic for falsifying one proposed internal block split, while the conditional characteristic-function modulus criterion remains available without moment assumptions; absence of detected variation never certifies atomicity. GoblerEtAl2024 and the Bosch analysis use supplied engineering groups and partial physical ground truth, not population-identified atomic units; the population theorem supplies the structural target for interpreting that grouping.
technical_internal_limitation: The three-coordinate crossing \(\{1,2\}\leftarrow\{3\}\) versus \(\{1,3\}\leftarrow\{2\}\) is the early kill test. Slice normalizers are positive and finite only on conull sets and are never differentiated. On each nonsingular inverse chart, the proof must pull back the conull regular sets, extend the fixed-base-point log-ratio identity from a conull dense subset by continuity, and derive path-independent chart gluing and critical-set continuation without fourth derivatives, analyticity, dominated differentiation, or primitive slice-integrability assumptions. Even if arbitrary crossings are excluded, partition equality still requires the separate strict-refinement quotient lemma. For a proposed process block, an internal directional ANM predicts conditional laws differing only by location and therefore constant conditional characteristic-function modulus and, when finite, constant conditional covariance. Detected variation falsifies that split; absence of detected variation does not prove atomicity. This is a domain interpretation, not theorem evidence from Bosch or any real data set. The quadratic Gaussian four-coordinate construction remains inadmissible because its middle-block innovations have explicit scalar ANM splits.
honest_scope: The triangular observed-density lemma makes strict positivity and \(C^3\) regularity of \(P\) derived consequences. The exact \(\operatorname{SmoothPos}\) definition, its nondegeneracy implication, the characteristic-function sufficient criterion, the one-direction covariance diagnostic, the empty-DAG lemma, the full-measure three-coordinate theorem, the open five-parameter vector-family lemma, and the atomicity-removal witness are solve targets. The covariance diagnostic is sufficient but not necessary, and a negative diagnostic does not certify atomicity. Arbitrary-block crossing rigidity and strict-refinement rigidity remain separate open obligations; partition uniqueness and headline recovery depend on both. Fixed-partition graph identification is a cited external fact from Corollary 1 of GoblerWindischDrton2025, and the linear-Gaussian reverse representation is a cited external fact from Example 24 of PetersEtAl2014; neither is a solve target. No finite certificate, density-space openness, genericity, consistency, rate, or finite-sample claim is made.
